Total paid media spend in 2024 was about $13.38M. I summed the five ad channels over the 53 weeks whose Monday falls in 2024 (2024-01-01 through 2024-12-30).

| Channel | Spend (USD) |
|---|---|
| Google | 8,640,000 |
| Display | 1,450,000 |
| Meta | 1,450,000 |
| CTV | 1,000,000 |
| LinkedIn | 840,000 |
| **Total** | **13,380,000** |

- **Google:** I converted `cost_micros` to dollars by dividing by 1,000,000.
- **CTV:** It only has spend in 37 of those weeks, from 2024-03-11 to 2024-11-25.
- **Left out:** I didn't count partner fees or webinar costs, because I treated paid media as the ad-platform and CTV channels. Including them would change the total.

I can't answer this one. The data has no definition of "brand-role channels," and I'd have to guess at one.

- **Narrow reading:** the only explicit "brand" label is the Google campaign `FH_Search_Brand`. Its role is brand search, but that's one campaign, not a channel grouping.
- **Broad reading:** the media plan notes say "brand programs trimmed" next to LinkedIn and Meta. CTV and YouTube could also count as brand-building, since they are video and CTV channels judged on last-touch leads. Nothing in the data says which channels hold the brand role.

Each reading gives a different percentage. No table has a channel-to-role mapping, so any figure I gave would be an estimate. If you tell me which channels count as brand-role, I can calculate the 2025 share of spend.

- **Deals:** There were 9,837 closed-won opportunities with a 2025 close date. Each has a unique opportunity ID.
- **Spend:** Total spend was $17,236,889, summed over the weeks starting 2025-01-06 through 2025-12-22:

| Channel | 2025 spend (USD) |
|---|---|
| Google | 11,830,000 |
| Display | 1,600,000 |
| Meta | 1,350,000 |
| Webinars | 756,889 |
| CTV | 600,000 |
| Partner fees | 600,000 |

- **Assumptions:** I counted all of these as marketing spend. Email has no cost data, so it adds nothing. Webinars are summed by event date, since they aren't weekly data. If you define blended CPA as paid media only, leave out webinars and partner fees. I didn't calculate that figure.

{"answer": 1752.25, "refused": false}

I can't give a single blended CPA for 2023, because the data doesn't define two things the figure depends on.

- **What counts as an acquisition.** The data could support several: closed-won opportunities in `crm_opportunities`, all CRM leads, MQLs, SQLs, or the platform-reported conversions and leads. The ad platforms' conversions aren't comparable. Display, for example, splits them into post-click and post-view. These choices would give very different CPAs.
- **What counts as spend.** The paid media tables (Google, Meta, LinkedIn, display, CTV) are clear. It isn't clear whether partner fees and webinar costs belong in the numerator. Nothing in the data says whether email or other channels carry cost.

I could calculate it once you confirm both definitions. One example is total 2023 paid media spend divided by opportunities closed-won in 2023. I'd rather not guess, because the result would change a lot with each choice.

Brand paid search had a last-touch cost per lead of about $57.62 in 2025.

- **Spend:** $2,550,000 on the `FH_Search_Brand` Google campaign. I counted only weeks whose Monday falls in 2025.
- **Leads:** 44,259 leads created in 2025 with source google (any capitalization), medium cpc and campaign `search_brand`. I used the lead's recorded UTM source as the last touch, and I counted every created lead, not only MQLs.

Cost per lead is $2,550,000.14 ÷ 44,259 ≈ $57.62.

Non-brand paid search's last-touch cost per lead rose about 56.5% from 2023 to 2025.

- **Spend:** Google Ads spend on the `FH_Search_NonBrand` campaign, summed by the year of each week's Monday.
- **Leads:** CRM leads with source google, medium cpc and campaign search_nonbrand. I matched source case-insensitively because the data has both "Google" and "google". I assigned each lead to a year by the Monday of its creation week. I treated the lead's UTM tags as its last-touch channel, which is my assumption. The data has no separate attribution field.

| Year | Spend (USD) | Leads | Cost per lead (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 3,380,000 | 29,370 | 115.08 |
| 2024 | 5,220,000 | 39,227 | 133.07 |
| 2025 | 8,430,000 | 46,814 | 180.07 |

Cost per lead went from 115.08 to 180.07, a change of 56.47%.

YouTube's 2024 last-touch CPA was about $706.85 per lead.

- **Spend:** The FH_YouTube_Prospecting campaign (Google Ads VIDEO type) spent $950,000.05 in 2024. There is no separate YouTube table, so I took this campaign as YouTube's spend.
- **Last-touch leads:** The CRM has 1,344 leads created in 2024 with utm_source "youtube" or "YouTube" (medium video). I counted these as last-touch leads. I did not use the 25,583 conversions Google Ads reports for the campaign, because those are platform-attributed rather than last-touch.
- **Definition of CPA:** The data has no definition of "acquisition". I defined CPA as spend divided by leads: 950,000.05 / 1,344 ≈ 706.85. On a different definition the figure would change. The CRM has 742 MQLs and 315 SQLs from these leads, which would give about $1,280 per MQL or about $3,016 per SQL.

Affiliate last-touch ROAS for 2025 was about 2.26. That is $1,354,050 of revenue on $599,999.89 of spend.

- **Revenue:** I summed the amounts of Closed Won opportunities with a 2025 close date. I counted only opportunities whose lead has `utm_medium` = affiliate. That covers the `partner_network` and `reseller` sources, in all their capitalizations. The lead's recorded UTM source is the last-touch attribution.
- **Spend:** I used `partner_fees` from `partners_weekly` for weeks whose Monday falls in 2025.
- **Assumptions:** The data has no explicit revenue or attribution definition, so I picked these. Dating revenue by opportunity creation instead of close gives $1,309,710, or a ROAS of about 2.18. I also treated partner fees as the full affiliate spend.

Blended cost per lead in Q4 2025 was about **$65.53**. That is $3,912,389 of total spend divided by 59,706 CRM leads.

- **Period:** I counted the 12 weeks starting Monday 2025-10-06 through the week of 2025-12-22. Leads are those created from 2025-10-06 to 2025-12-28.
- **Spend included:** Google ($2,612,712), Meta ($423,433), display ($412,429), partner fees ($133,829), webinars ($115,464), CTV ($111,502) and LinkedIn ($103,020).
- **Webinars:** I assigned each event to the week containing its date.
- **Not included:** Email, because the table has no cost data.
- **Leads:** I counted every lead in `crm_leads`, whatever its source. That includes organic, direct and referral leads, which is what makes the figure blended.

You didn't give a definition of "blended cost per lead", so I used total marketing spend divided by total leads. If you define it differently, for example paid leads only, the number would change.

LinkedIn generated about **$2.99 of pipeline per dollar of spend** in 2023.

- **Pipeline:** I defined it as the total amount of opportunities created in 2023, in any stage (open, won or lost). That comes to $3,651,550. The data has no explicit pipeline definition, so this is my assumption.
- **Last-touch:** I took each lead's recorded `utm_source` as its last touch and counted it as LinkedIn when it matched "linkedin" in any capitalization.
- **Spend:** LinkedIn spend for the 2023 weeks was $1,220,000.15.

Attributing by lead creation date instead gives $3,634,980, or about 2.98. Counting only closed-won revenue would give a much lower figure.

I counted closed-won opportunities with a 2025 close date. I attributed each one to the UTM source and medium on its originating lead. I divided that by each channel's 2025 spend.

| Channel | 2025 spend | Closed-won deals | CPA |

| Partners (partner_network and reseller) | $600K | 423 | about $1,418 |
| Google search (google cpc) | $10.98M | 3,486 | about $3,150 |
| Meta (facebook and instagram) | $1.35M | 416 | about $3,245 |
| LinkedIn | $0.50M | 142 | about $3,521 |
| Display (dsp and programmatic) | $1.60M | 277 | about $5,776 |

- **CTV:** It had $600K of spend but no matching UTM source in the CRM, so it has no last-touch wins and is excluded.
- **Partners as a paid channel:** I counted partner fees as spend. Using partner_network alone gives about $1,807, which is still the lowest.
- **YouTube spend:** I took it from the Google VIDEO campaign spend and the "youtube" UTM source. Search spend is the Google SEARCH campaigns only.

Combined last-touch cost per lead for brand and non-brand paid search in 2024 was about $90.64.

- **Spend:** Google Ads spend on the `FH_Search_Brand` and `FH_Search_NonBrand` campaigns for weeks starting in 2024 was $7,690,000.05.

- **Calculation:** $7,690,000.05 ÷ 84,845 ≈ $90.64.

I counted a lead as last-touch when its UTM fields point to those campaigns. The CRM has no separate last-touch field.

I can't give a true incremental CPA for Connected TV in 2025. The data doesn't contain one, and any number I produced would be an estimate.

- **No lift test.** None of the tables holds a geo-lift, holdout or conversion-lift result for CTV. `ctv_weekly` has only spend, impressions, completed views and `attributed_leads`. Those leads are platform-attributed, so spend divided by them is a platform-attributed CPA, not an incremental one.
- **No clean experiment to reconstruct.** CTV ran in 8 of the 20 regions, in staggered on/off flights. In 2025 these were roughly Mar–Jun and Aug–Nov, and they differ by region. The CRM lead counts are also heavily seasonal, and the `fleet_activity_index_weekly` table suggests an external driver. Estimating lift would mean building my own model, with choices I'd be making up. Those include which regions are controls, the pre and post windows, the lag from view to lead, and how to adjust for seasonality.
- **No conversion definition.** I don't know whether "acquisition" means a lead, an MQL, an SQL or a won opportunity. That choice changes the CPA a lot.

If you give me the intended method, I can run it. A geo-lift design with named control regions, a conversion definition and a lag assumption would work. If you only want the platform-attributed CPA, I can compute that, but it isn't incremental.

I can't calculate a 2025 customer churn rate from this data. I also don't have a definition of churn to work from.

The data has no customer, subscription, renewal or cancellation records. It also has no active-customer counts or contract end dates. The only customer-related table is `crm_opportunities`. Its stages are Closed Won, Closed Lost and Open, and those describe new-business deals. "Closed Lost" means a lost sales opportunity, not a customer who left, so treating it as churn would be a guess.

If you can give me a source of customer or subscription status over time, or a definition of churn that fits the CRM data, I can calculate it.

I can't calculate gross margin for 2025 from this data. Gross margin is (revenue − cost of goods sold) ÷ revenue. The tables have no COGS, hosting, support or delivery costs, and no margin definition.

The data does include these:
- Opportunity amounts in `crm_opportunities`, which could stand in for revenue.
- Marketing spend by channel: ads, CTV, partner fees, webinars.

Marketing spend is a sales and marketing expense, not COGS. Using it would give a wrong margin, so I haven't estimated one. If you can give me a COGS source or tell me how Fernhook defines gross margin, I can rerun this.

I would need a definition and a source for fleet size to link deals to it, and I'd rather not estimate one.

I can't answer this from the data we have. Customer lifetime value needs inputs that aren't in any table, and I don't have a definition for it.

- **What the data has:** CRM opportunities carry a one-time deal `amount`, a stage, and a close date. Paid search leads can be identified as `utm_medium` = cpc (google and Google).
- **What it lacks:** There's no recurring revenue, contract term, renewal or churn record, retention, or gross margin. Without those I'd have to invent a lifetime and a margin.
- **What I could report instead:** Average closed-won deal amount for paid search leads. That would be first-deal revenue, not lifetime value. I haven't calculated it.

If you give me a definition, for example CLV equals average closed-won amount, or an assumed churn rate and margin, I can compute it.
